notes.title: Inflation, Help or Demise?
notes.content:
[p][b]Hello Traders,
[/b][/p][p]Inflation is a big topic in Trade Conquest that always brings up questions. Here is a quick list of what factors affect it followed by a detailed breakdown for each point. [/p][p][/p][p][b]Inflation is a combination of:[/b][/p][p][b]1.[/b] The average Demand in goods for Agriculture, Meats, Alcohol, Luxury, Infrastructure, Crude Oil, Natural Gas, Gasoline and Diesel resources for your Home Market.[/p][p][b]2.[/b] Debt and Economy development confidence measured by your Interest rates.[/p][p][b]3.[/b] Counterfeit (If applicable).[/p][p][b]4.[/b] Sudden increase in GDP, 10% or higher.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45167306/1c838622f00b2d54f34e064a485254b6fec8b276.png"][/img][/p][p][b]Positives and Negatives[/b] [/p][p]
-Inflation affects prices for buildings and Industries purchased not only by yourself as a business person, but for the nation as well, hurting their development for the need to pay higher prices. 
-Increases Maintenance costs in proportion to inflation. 
-On GDP growth:[/p][list][*][p]0% to -10% Inflation: No effect on GDP growth.[/p][/*][*][p]Greater than 0% to 5% Inflation: The sweet spot for optimal GDP growth.[/p][/*][*][p]Greater than 5% to under 10% Inflation: No effect on GDP growth.[/p][/*][/list][list][*][p]10%+ Inflation: Begins to negatively impact GDP growth, with significant penalties at very high levels.[/p][/*][/list][p]-Possible unrest events like protests because of High Unrest.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45167306/05d69895921796ebeb6546cd50144191dfaca2f9.png"][/img][/p][p][b]Where to find the current inflation information[/b][/p][p]-Left click on a province, it’ll show on the top left along with Corporate Tax. 
-Right click on a nation’s province, it’ll show in an Information window. 
-Oval Office tab under “taxation” for your Home country.[/p][h2]1. [/h2][p]-The average Demand of the listed “Essential” goods can reach a low end of -75%. Although trying to meet the high demand would be Ideal, lowering prices for other goods would also have the same affects, even if you do not make as much profit from them as you would like.[/p][p]-Do like many Major nations do, make a Business Agreement. Exploit other nation’s essential resources and sell it at your own market. An Undeveloped Economy might mean cheaper labor costs as well as new goods to exploit. 
-In the Market Tab, Lock your higher tier resources, (The ones giving you the most profits) and sell them where there is most demand after you have Force Liquidated all essential goods at your Home Market to make sure demand is kept low. (Or sell 1 by 1 for the most profit) 
-You can also purchase the needed goods from a market with low demand, and sell it to yours on Next Quarter. If you sell it the same Quarter you’ll get Market Manipulation penalties.[/p][p]-Gasoline and Diesel are also important because higher demand will also increase your transportation costs.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45167306/30188b0da939a380df7fd4b8db5176e400d9ab01.png"][/img][/p][h2]2.[/h2][p]A Developed Economy will naturally have more resistance to inflation than Undeveloped Economies. 
If your debt goes beyond your nation’s GDP, you will have an exponential inflation increase. Inflation is adjusted Monthly and if big changes are made, will adjust gradually over time.[/p][p]How to Lower Debt if not Head of State: 
-Higher Tier Industries: Increases Corporate Taxes revenue and Gross Domestic Product per Capital (GDPPC), which can mean higher Income tax revenue. 
-Infrastructure such as Highways, Trains and Airports: Increases Investments Revenue.
-Build Banks and Financial Districts: Increases Corporate Taxes Revenue.[/p][p]Pay Debt (When Head of State): Use your personal account to pay national debt. This will help improve inflation at the end of the year when budgets are re balanced. [/p][h2]3.[/h2][p]Opposing nations can carry out several Special Operations against your nation, just like you can. The “Counterfeit” operation can increase your inflation up to a maximum of +50%. This is on top of your base levels. You can pass a bill to help clean things up. It will however, naturally fall over time, faster on more Developed economies.[/p][h2]4.[/h2][p]If you have a sudden increase of GDP by 10% or higher, through High Tier Industries purchases or Conquest, this influx will be reflected on your inflation until the end of the year, and fall gradually over time afterwards.[/p][p]
I hope this information helps newcomers and veterans alike.
[/p][p][b]Best,[/b]
[b]GrandPaw Games[/b][/p]

notes.title: 🌏 Big Update: Beautiful World Mode, Labor Costs & More!
notes.content:
Hey Traders,

We’re thrilled to bring you the Beautiful World update—packed with features to expand your Trade Conquest experience. This update will affect save files, so prepare for a fresh start to enjoy everything new and avoid any issues!

Key Features Coming:
[b]Beautiful World Game Mode (New!)[/b]
[list]
[*] Customize nations before playing: Edit Territories, GDP, Population, Names, Traits and much more.
[*] 10 Additional Historical Nations have been added to this list that can only been edited and played as through this Game Mod. Includes Confederate States, Soviet Union and Third Reich.
[*] Perfect for alternate histories or challenge runs to create your own Beautiful World. 
[*] Note: Separate save slot | No achievements or ranking.[/list]

[b]Dynamic Labor Costs[/b]
Maintenance costs now scale with GDPPC:
[list]
[*] High-income (Developed Economy) (50K+ GDPPC): +50% labor costs
[*] Middle-income (Developed Economy) (15K-50K): Gradual 0% to +50%
[*] Lower-middle (Emerging Economy) (4K-15K): -25% to 0% discount
[*] Low-income (Undeveloped Economy) (<4K): Permanent -25% discount [/list]
Nations with strong Labor Unions like Nordic nations now start with "Labor Union" law (+10% Labor Costs and -0.1 monthly unrest in all provinces/territories).
Complimentary new research further reduces unrest by 0.05.

This is to help give the feel of "Cheaper Labor" in underdeveloped nations and higher expenses in "Developed Nations" with its own pros and cons. 

[b]New Ranking[/b]
World Ranking for [i]Economy[/i] Win-Con: New World Order based on the least number of days taken to achieve Economy Win. 

[b]Quality of Life[/b]
[list]
[*] Market Search Bar: Find resources instantly (exact spelling required).
[*] Strict Resource Locking: Locked resources at the Market Tab won’t sell— even via auto-sell/liquidation. (✓/✗)
[*] Political Map Colors: Num-9 now swaps both map and bill colors for left/right leanings.
[/list]

[b]Accessibility & Immersion[/b]
German & Spanish language support added. Options in Main menu and Game menu. 
Other languages in the works. Let us know your interests as a Comment or in our Discord!
New current events reflecting modern times.

[b]Bug Fixes & Balancing[/b]
AI combat patterns reworked.
Military Resources Demand based on Wars increased.
Private Security now provides an additional 0.01 Monthly Unrest Reduction
HUD adjustments to better fit languages. 
And as always, we’ve squashed bugs and fine-tuned other mechanics for gameplay.

⚠️ Important: This update will affect saved games. We recommend wrapping up ongoing campaigns before updating to avoid any issues.

How to YouTube Video link Below: 
[previewyoutube=hacwUs-XBe0;full][/previewyoutube]

Let us know your experiences and Alternate History! 

Best,
GrandPaw Games

notes.title: 🌍 Update: United Europe Movement, New Laws & More!
notes.content:
Hey Traders,

We’re excited to bring you another update packed with new features, improvements, and fixes! This update focuses on deepening the political and economic systems in Trade Conquest, while also addressing performance and stability. Here’s everything you need to know:

[b]United Europe Movement:[/b]
[list]
[*] A new “United Europe Movement” has been added under the “Business” province tab.
[*] This movement is only available for EU member states and can be accessed in their Capital Province.
[*] Fund the movement to accelerate its progress toward unifying the EU into a single nation.
[*] Success requires high support from each member state, which shifts monthly.
[/list]
[b]New EU Candidate:[/b]
Georgia has been added as an EU candidate starting December 14, 2023.

[b]New Social Laws for Continental Europe:[/b]
Two new social laws have been added for Continental European nations:
[list]
[*] Become an EU Candidate: Apply for EU membership if your nation is not already a candidate.
[*] Join a United Europe: Become part of a successful United Europe movement, giving up your Head of State status if applicable.
[/list]
Note: These additions are not available in the “End of Empires” game mode.

[b]Debt-to-GDP Unrest Consequences:[/b]

High debt-to-GDP ratios now have negative unrest consequences:
[list]
[*] 2x GDP: +0.02 Unrest
[*] 5x GDP: +0.05 Unrest
[*] 10x GDP+: +0.1 Unrest
[/list]

notes.title: 🌍 Major Update is Live: GDP Overhaul, Modern Politics & More!
notes.content:
Hello Traders,

[b]The major update is now live[/b], and it’s packed with features that will transform your [i]Trade Conquest [/i]experience! From a reworked GDP system to modernized politics and a sleek new “Phone” interface, there’s something for everyone. As a reminder, this update will affect save files, so dive in fresh to experience all the new changes (New game is a must for things to work correctly).

Here’s everything you need to know:

[b]Reworked GDP Growth System:[/b]
GDP growth is now calculated on a per-province basis, with its effects being added or subtracted monthly. Multiple factors influence it:

1. Industry Tiers: Higher tiers (starting at T2) provide greater GDP growth, while Tier 1 provides none. 

2. Inflation:
[list]
[*] 0% to -10% Inflation: No effect on GDP growth.
[*] Greater than 0% to 5% Inflation: The sweet spot for optimal GDP growth.
[*] Greater than 5% to under 10% Inflation: No effect on GDP growth.
[*] 10%+ Inflation: Begins to negatively impact GDP growth, with significant penalties at very high levels.
[/list]
3. Production Bonuses: Laws that provide production bonuses will increase GDP growth per province, while negative production bonuses will decrease it.

4. Province Stability: Provinces can experience negative growth with high unrest.

5. National Growth: Achieving 10%+ yearly growth (rare and often through conquest or by smaller nations) will initially spike inflation but balance over time.

6. New Laws: Laws are a great way to increase GDP growth if you can balance the negative effects.

[b]Modernized Politics:[/b]
The Politics tab is now divided into Economy, Social, and Security with a new display bar showing how much Influence you currently have for the selected nation from the maximum. A new mechanic introduces [b]“The People”[/b] and [b]“Corporate”[/b] support:

Pass laws aligned with either group to gain their support.
Maintain 75+ support from one group for a 5% monthly influence bonus, or 15% if both groups are at 75+. Support is reduced over time. 

To pass the “Enabling Act” and become head of state, you now also need at least 75+ support from either “The People” or “Corporate” groups, in addition to the previous requirements.

[b]Economy Win Condition:[/b]
A new victory path! Achieve 55% of the world’s GDP before any other nation to claim economic dominance. An achievement has been added to celebrate this milestone.

[b]New Phone who dis?:[/b]
[list]
[*] The new Phone UI replaces the Current Events and Notifications system.
[*] It consolidates all current events and notifications into one place.
[*] View the date, clear notifications individually or all at once, and revisit past events.
[*] The Phone icon glows blue when new information is available.
[/list]
Access it via the bottom-right button. Note: This does not replace general pop-ups, only current events and notifications.

[b]New Playable Nations:[/b]
USA, Russia, China, and India are now playable starting nations in the “New World Order” game mode. Lead these global superpowers to dominance!

[b]New Disaster Categories:[/b]
Disasters are now categorized into:
[list]
[*] Recent Disasters (mostly natural disasters with it's affects lasting 3 months),
[*] Pandemics ( with it's affects lasting 6 months),
[*] Vermin Infestations (localized but persistent, will start removal once unrest has been reduced).
[/list]
[b]Dynamic Events:[/b]
New “Avatar” events to better highlight character backgrounds and more dynamic event options to shape your story. So choose wisely. 

[b]Production in Tons:[/b]
Production values are now displayed in Tons to match market prices, with storage amounts adjusted accordingly for a more intuitive experience.

[b]Quality of Life Additions:[/b]
[list]
[*] New “Diplomacy” Button: Quickly navigate to a nation’s diplomacy tab from the Province menu.
[*] Force Liquidation: Sell all resources at once in the Market Tab for a fee. (Hover for additional details)
[*] Disband Missiles: Decommission ICBMs and Hypersonic Missiles from your reserves as head of state.
[*] Music Tab: Enjoy additional tracks to keep the Jazz and Chill vibes alive during long sessions.
[*] Right-Click Ocean: Close nation information windows by right-clicking the ocean, just like left-clicking closes tabs.
[*] Window Mode Improvements: Keeps music playing when clicking outside the game.
[*] Bulldoze Flexibility: Bulldoze different tier industries in sequence, including all higher tiers.
[*] New Climate: “Monsoon Tropical” added to better represent South East Asia’s spice trade.
[/list]

[b]Bug Fixes & Balancing:[/b]
[*] Crude Oil and Gas: Because of their importance in electricity, heating and a cornerstone in so many higher tier resources, Crude Oil and Natural Gas have been added to the "Inflation Average" list. Their demand in your Home Market will now affect your inflation.
[*] Inflation Capped: Now ranges from -10% to 1000%.

As always, we’ve squashed bugs and fine-tuned gameplay for a smoother experience.

We’re thrilled to bring these changes to you and can’t wait to see how you shape the world in your vision.

Thank you for your continued support, and happy trading!

Best,
GrandPaw Games

notes.title: Get Ready for the Playtest: Power, Strategy, and Economic Domination
notes.content:
Dear Gamers,

We’re excited to announce the upcoming [b]Trade Conquest playtest[/b]! As you prepare to dive into the game, here are some key features and mechanics to familiarize yourself with, spread across several important tabs. For more detailed information, head to the Knowledge Tab inside the game.

[h2]Provinces:[/h2]
[b]Inflation and Taxes: [/b]Purchases within a province are influenced by national inflation and corporate taxes.
[b]GDP Boost:[/b] Resources and industries increase provincial GDP, minus taxes and inflation.
[b]Storage: [/b]Be mindful of how much you can store—excess resources go to waste.
[b]Projects/Investments: [/b]Expensive but impactful long-term investments.
[b]Flags: [/b]Display ownership of resource lots; your avatar will show on your owned lots.
[b]Building Times: [/b]Ranges from 8 to 68 months depending on tier.
[h2]Trade Tab:[/h2]
[b]Markets:[/b] Most markets are open unless events disrupt them.
[b]Sell Carefully: [/b]Lack of resources will cost you 4x the base value on auto-purchases.
[b]Logistics Fees:[/b] Included with all purchases.
[b]Fluctuation: [/b]Flooding markets with resources lowers demand and prices.
[b]Highlighted Resources:[/b] Easily spot what you produce in markets.
[b]Demand Fluctuation: [/b]Events and wars significantly affect demand.
[h2]Research Tab:[/h2]
All research knowledge can be acquired from the Investment window in each province or by passing certain bills.
[b]Business Research:[/b] Improves maintenance, building, and purchasing efficiency.
[b]Social Research: [/b]Enhances production, influence, and unrest management.
[b]Military Research:[/b] Increases unit effectiveness, production speed, and other key stats.
[h2]Politics Tab:[/h2]
[b]Political Leaning:[/b] Government types impact the laws and business environment.
[b]Influence:[/b] Use money to gain influence and pass beneficial laws.
[b]Consolidated Power:[/b] Pass the “Enabling Act” to become Head of State, giving you full control over your nation but with added risks.
[h2]Military Tab:[/h2]
[b]Effectiveness & Manpower:[/b] Track unit strength and available manpower.
[b]Maintenance Costs: [/b]Units cost upkeep whether in reserves or active.
[b]Create Units & Armies:[/b] Requires resources, and units appear at the capital.
[b]Army View: [/b]Provides full details on your forces, including traits, moves, and autonomy settings.
[h2]Diplomacy Tab:[/h2]
[b]Relations & War: [/b]Manage alliances, declare war, and give aid to improve relationships.
[b]Alliances: [/b]You can have 1-2 allies, and they’ll support you in war.
[b]Sanctions: [/b]Harm relations and cut off market access.
[h2]Oval Office:[/h2]
[b]GDP and Population Stats: [/b]GDP per capita and unrest metrics influence immigration and workforce.
[b]Unrest: [/b]Manage unrest to avoid serious workforce reductions and negative effects.
[b]Debt and Inflation: [/b]Pay national debt to improve inflation over time.
For those looking to dive deeper, the [i][b]Knowledge Tab[/b][/i] has a wealth of additional information to explore.

[b]Be sure to join our Discord for feedback and to share your experiences during the playtest:[/b]
[url=https://discord.gg/JFRCZP6sXW]Discord Invite[/url]

Best,
GrandPaw Games

notes.title: Unveil the Resource Secrets Hidden in Every Province’s Climate!
notes.content:
Dear Gamers,

We’re excited to share more about how climates will affect resource availability in [b]Trade Conquest[/b]. Our game offers a dynamic approach to resource distribution, where provinces will be randomly assigned up to 12 different resources, depending on the [b]climate[/b]. Although a few exceptions may allow some preset resources in unexpected climates, most provinces will follow the guidelines below—so be sure to plan accordingly as you expand!

Additionally, keep in mind that the further you build from your capital, the higher your transportation costs will be. Every playthrough brings unique challenges as you won’t know exactly what to expect with each new game.

Here’s a breakdown of where you can expect to find resources based on the climate:

[h3]Tropical Rainforest[/h3]
[b]Mining, Oil and Gas:[/b]
Gold, Silver, Iron, Nickel, Titanium, Copper, Calcium, Crude Oil, Natural Gas, Bauxite, Diamonds
[b]Agriculture:[/b]
Bananas, Cattle, Coconut, Cocoa, Cotton, Coffee, Exotic Woods, Fish, Lumber, Pineapple, Pork, Poultry, Rubber, Silk, Soybeans, Sugar, Water
[b]Flexible:[/b]
Glass, Aspergillus Terrus
[h3]Tropical Savanna[/h3]
[b]Mining, Oil and Gas:[/b]
Iron, Nickel, Titanium, Copper, Calcium, Bauxite, Diamonds
[b]Agriculture:[/b]
Bananas, Cattle, Coconut, Cotton, Cocoa, Coffee, Exotic Woods, Fish, Lumber, Pineapple, Pork, Poultry, Rubber, Soybeans, Sugar, Water
[b]Flexible:[/b]
Glass, Aspergillus Terrus, MJ Leaves
[h3]Arid[/h3]
[b]Mining, Oil and Gas:[/b]
Iron, Titanium, Lithium, Uranium, Graphite, Copper, Crude Oil, Natural Gas, Fluorite, Calcium, Silica Stone
[b]Agriculture:[/b]
Goats, Pork, Poultry, Sheep, Aloe, Lavender 
[b]Flexible:[/b]
Salt, Asphalt, Glass
[h3]Semiarid[/h3]

Iron, Titanium, Copper, Crude Oil, Natural Gas, Lithium, Silica Stone, Silver, Fluorite, Calcium, Graphite, Bauxite

Cattle, Cotton, Goats, Pork, Poultry, Sheep, Soybeans, Wheat, Corn, Aloe, Lavender

Asphalt, Glass, Salt
[h3]Moderate Dry[/h3]
[b]Mining, Oil and Gas:[/b]
Iron, Copper, Calcium
[b]Agriculture:[/b]
Apples, Cotton, Goats, Grapes, Lemon, Olives, Oranges, Pork, Poultry, Sheep, Spices, Wheat, Corn, Sugar, Potatoes, Aloe, Lavender

Opium Poppy, Glass, Aspergillus Terrus, Penicillium, MJ Leaves
[h3]Moderate Humid[/h3]

Iron, Copper
[b]Agriculture:[/b]
Apples, Cotton, Exotic Woods, Grapes, Goats, Lumber, Mint, Olives, Lemon, Oranges, Pork, Poultry, Sheep, Spices, Wheat, Corn, Sugar

Glass, Penicillium, Opium Poppy, Aspergillus Terrus, MJ Leaves, Asphalt

Apples, Grapes, Cattle, Goats, Lumber, Mint, Pork, Poultry, Sheep, Wheat, Corn, Potatoes
[b]Flexible:[/b]
Penicillium, MJ Leaves
[h3]Continental Long[/h3]
[b]Mining, Oil and Gas:[/b]
Iron, Coal, Copper, Graphite, Silver, Fluorite, Calcium
[b]Agriculture:[/b]
Apples, Cattle, Goats, Grapes, Lumber, Pork, Poultry, Sheep, Wheat, Corn, Potatoes

Penicillium, Opium Poppy, MJ Leaves

[b]Mining, Oil and Gas:[/b]
Iron, Coal, Copper, Graphite, Calcium, Silver, Fluorite, Uranium
[b]Agriculture:[/b]
Apples, Cattle, Goats, Lumber, Pork, Poultry, Sheep, Wheat, Corn, Potatoes 
[h3]Grasslands[/h3]
[b]Mining, Oil and Gas:[/b]
Copper, Iron, Coal
[b]Agriculture:[/b]
Cattle, Goat, Sheep, Pork, Poultry, Fish, Water, Soybeans, Wheat, Corn, Cotton, Potatoes

[b]Agriculture:[/b]
Apples, Coffee, Cotton, Grapes, Lemons, Olives, Oranges, Cattle, Goats, Pork, Poultry, Sheep, Spices, Llamas, Water, Potatoes 
[b]Flexible:[/b]

[h3]Highlands[/h3]

Thank you for your continued support, and happy strategizing!

Best,
GrandPaw Games
